items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to the purchase of
domestically produced personal protective equipment
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4110

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to the purchase of
domestically produced personal protective equipment

 
PURPOSE:

To require a New York State manufactured and produced stockpile of
personal protective equipment for all agencies to utilize in the event
of a health emergency or crisis.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This legislation requires any agencies purchasing personal protective
equipment to utilize New York State owned businesses through the exist-
ing preferred source program for at least thirty percent of the total
amount purchased. A definition for what qualifies as personal protective
equipment is also created.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Recent health emergencies have shown that state agencies need a stock-
pile of personal protective equipment in order to deal with crises as
quickly as they emerge. As New York begins the process of preparing for
the next emergency, it is critical that these products be produced
domestically and within State whenever practicable. This requirement
will provide a trusted chain of custody of the products, as well as
creating economic opportunities within the State. The current preferred
source program creates incredible opportunities for the historically
under-served workforce of individuals with disabilities who can readily
meet these new demands for production of personal protective equipment.
In these times of economic uncertainty, requiring certain amounts of
personal protective equipment to be produced through the preferred
source program will help the businesses that employ these individuals
with a necessary life preserver to remain open and serving the people of
New York.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019/2020: S8646 - Referred to Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  Minimal.   
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law and the public authorities law, in
relation to the purchase of personal protective equipment and medical supplies
produced or manufactured in the state of New York
A.lawCode: Amd §148, St Fin L; amd §2878-c, Pub Auth L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4110A

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law and the public authorities law, in
relation to the purchase of personal protective equipment and medical
supplies produced or manufactured in the state of New York

 
PURPOSE:

To require a New York State manufactured and produced personal protec-
tive equipment and medical supplies in certain state contracts, and to
establish preferred sourcing requirements on certain contracts for New
York State manufactured or produced personal protective equipment (PPE)
or medical supplies items.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the State Finance Law, to require state agency
contracts valued at over $50,000 for the purchase of PPE or medical
supplies items, utilize PPE or medical supplies made either in whole or
in part in New York State; requires 30 percent of such PPE or medical
supplies items be sourced from preferred sources in accordance with
section one hundred sixty-two of the State Finance Law.

Section 2 amends the Public Authorities Law, to require state public
authority contracts valued at over $50,000 for the purchase of PPE or
medical supplies items, utilize PPE or medical supplies made either in
whole or in part in New York State; requires 30 percent of such PPE or
medical supplies items be sourced from preferred sources in accordance
with section one hundred sixty-two of the State Finance Law.

Section 3 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This proposal was amended to reflect the changes made to the State
Finance Law from the passage of the New York Medical Supplies Act.  This
proposal now applies to all contracts for PPE or medical supplies valued
at over $50,000. Under this new version of the proposal, if PPE or
medical supplies items made in New York State, in the United States, or
by a preferred source is unavailable, any other domestically-located
business may be utilized to satisfy the requirements set by the
proposal. The proposal's effective date was also amended, to now take
effect 60 days after becoming law. Finally, the proposal now applies to
any state contracting opportunities advertised on or after that date.
The proposal explicitly now excludes contracts for which an invitation
for bid, request for proposal, or similar solicitation is issued prior
to it becoming law.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: New Bill/Similar Bill: S.8646/Breslin - Died in Rules
2020: New Bill/Same-as Bill: A. 10691/Rules (McDonald) - Died in Govern-
mental Operations

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall apply to any state contracting opportunities
advertised on or after such date and shall exclude contracts for which
an invitation for bid, request for proposal, or similar solicitation has
been issued prior to this proposal becoming effective.
